payload.name: Preserve Distinct Events on Update
payload.description: When updating or merging memories during CRUD, if a new message describes a different event than the existing memory, even for the same person, keep both as separate memories instead of overwriting.
content: During CRUD, before applying UPDATE or MERGE to an existing memory, determine whether the incoming evidence describes the same real-world event or a distinct event. Distinct if the event type, time, or occurrence differs (e.g., pregnancy vs marriage announcement).
If the events are distinct, do not overwrite or replace the existing memory. ADD a separate memory for the new event and retain the old one intact.

Only UPDATE/MERGE when the new information truly corrects or extends the same event (e.g., a more precise date or explicit retraction). Do not assume same subject or near timing implies the same event.
After preserving the distinct event, stop; do not create redundant copies of the same new event.

solves: Prevents loss of previously stored facts when a later message describes a new event related to the same person or partner. Construction agents sometimes overwrite an existing event memory with a different event that shares the same subject or close timing, erasing the original fact.
